workflow_hypothesis: Concurrent diagnostic traversal dereferences released execution state
pattern: Concurrent traversal uses runtime-owned records without stable references or teardown exclusion
description: A diagnostic or serialization traversal reads shared runtime state while another execution context can mutate, release, or destroy that state. Because the traversal does not establish a stable snapshot, ownership, or exclusion interval, references obtained during traversal may be invalidated before later fields or values are processed.
precondition: A worker traverses interpreter-managed records or container-owned entries whose lifetime and contents can be changed by another thread, and the traversal retains borrowed or otherwise non-owning access across multiple operations.
critical_operation: The traversal obtains a record, entry, iterator position, or associated metadata and proceeds toward formatting, reference acquisition, or serialization without first holding the synchronization or ownership needed to stabilize the traversed state.
interference: Another thread concurrently mutates the container or tears down the execution context, releasing, replacing, or destroying the state that the traversal observed.
invalid_assumption: The observed record or borrowed entry will remain valid until the traversal finishes using it, even though no stable snapshot, ownership transfer, critical section, global interpreter lock, or stop-the-world boundary covers the observation-to-use interval.
failure: Later traversal accesses read freed or otherwise invalid runtime state, causing a process-terminating segmentation fault or memory-safety failure instead of a safe concurrent-modification or teardown outcome.
search_strategy: Inspect diagnostic, serialization, and inspection traversals of shared runtime state for borrowed records or entries that are used after the retrieval step.
Verify that record traversal is enclosed by an appropriate lock, interpreter-state attachment, global runtime lock, stop-the-world barrier, or equivalent stable-snapshot mechanism.
Trace concurrent mutation and teardown paths for entry removal, replacement, interpreter destruction, execution-record release, and metadata reclamation during traversal.
Check every observation-to-use interval, including formatting and reference acquisition, for a race between reading a non-owning handle and making it owned or consuming its fields.
Distinguish container mutation races from execution-context teardown races and confirm that each has a matching lifetime and synchronization guarantee.

evidence.supports: A serializer retrieved borrowed mapping entries and attempted to retain or process them while another thread could remove or replace those entries; enclosing retrieval and retention in a critical section prevents invalidation.

scope_note: Membership was manually restricted to the evidence listed below. Two mechanisms share an unstable traversal boundary: runtime-record teardown during diagnostic collection, and container mutation between borrowed-entry retrieval and ownership acquisition. Apply this pattern only where a traversal lacks the exclusion, snapshot, or lifetime protection required by the observed reference.
